---
title: "Choose a quantization"
---

`quantization_us` is the only lossy knob in spikepack — it trades maximum timing
error against size. The error introduced is bounded and predictable: at most half
a tick.

| `quantization_us` | Worst-case error | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `25` | ≤ 12.5 µs | close to raw sorter precision; larger deltas, less compressible |
| `50` | ≤ 25 µs | conservative default if you're unsure |
| `100` | ≤ 50 µs | frozen default for IBL `bwm_ephys`; good fidelity/size tradeoff for PSTH/event-alignment analyses |
| `250` | ≤ 125 µs | smallest files; only if downstream analysis truly doesn't need sub-ms precision |

## Profile it on your own data

Compression ratio depends on firing rate (denser trains → smaller deltas → better
ratios) and on how much of the signal is genuinely random vs. bursty/rhythmic, so
the right value can differ from IBL's. Profile a few settings on a representative
sample before committing to one:

```python
import numpy as np
from spikepack import encode_times, compress_array

for q in (25, 50, 100, 250):
    deltas, meta = encode_times(times, quantization_us=q)
    payload, spec = compress_array(deltas)
    print(f"{q:>4} us  ->  dtype={meta['dtype']:<6}  "
          f"compressed={len(payload):,} B  "
          f"CR={times.nbytes / len(payload):.1f}x")
```

Keep the chosen value consistent within one dataset release, and always record it
in the container's metadata (`write_blosc`/`write_zarr` do this automatically via
`meta["quantization_us"]`) — a reader has no way to recover it otherwise.
